hook: Rabinovich arrived at the Longuet-Higgins Prize, the computer vision field's highest honor for work that has stood the test of time, the same year his startup was acquired and he became CTO of a public company. His arc from Google research to Magic Leap's human-centered AR, to founding an AI meeting tool, to leading AI at one of the world's largest freelance platforms is a compressed version of the field's own evolution: from perception research to multimodal generation to enterprise deployment.
name: Andrew Rabinovich

quote.text: Special focus on Human Centered AI and Experiential Learning.

moniker: CTO and Head of AI at Upwork

reading.body:
Rabinovich received the Longuet-Higgins Prize, computer vision's highest honor for enduring research, in the same year his acquired startup made him CTO of a public company, placing foundational academic recognition and commercial deployment in the same moment.

His trajectory runs in a single direction: from perception research at UC San Diego and Google, through embodied AR at Magic Leap, to a meeting platform he co-founded and then sold, to leading AI strategy at one of the world's largest freelance marketplaces. Each move adds a layer, from low-level image understanding to multimodal systems to enterprise software products. The sequence reflects how computer vision research, once confined to classification and segmentation tasks, became load-bearing infrastructure inside products used at scale.

What the data does not cover is the technical architecture of what Upwork now runs, how Headroom's meeting-platform work was absorbed into it, or what compute resources underpin those systems. His stated focus on human-centered AI and experiential learning appears on his LinkedIn profile but is not elaborated further here. The record is strong on career structure and recognition, thin on the engineering specifics that would connect his work to questions of compute, power, or deployment infrastructure.
